predecessors.name: Zhou dynasty
predecessors.text: the Wei River valley, evacuated by the Zhou court after the sack of Fenghao in 771 (Western Zhou page)

successors.name: Qin (state)
successors.text: 'the former Zhou land' the Rong occupied until Duke Wen of Qin's victory of 750; Qin kept the part west of Qishan

ledger.x: 771: the Quanrong, invited by the Marquess of Shen, storm the Zhou capital.
766: Duke Xiang of Qin dies fighting the Quanrong at Qishan.
750: Duke Wen of Qin breaks the Rong.
750: the Rong lose the Wei valley to Qin.
750: the Rong hold of the Wei valley ends, and with it this dossier.

wars.name: Sack of Fenghao
wars.outcome: The rebel Marquis of Shen, Zeng and the Quanrong defeated King You's army at Mount Li and sacked the capital; the king was killed and the court moved east, ending the Western Zhou.

wars.name: Qin wars against the Rong
wars.outcome: Qin, 'the westernmost of the Zhou states, bore the brunt of the fighting against the Rong'; Duke Xiang died fighting the Quanrong at Qishan in 766, and Duke Wen defeated the Rong occupying the former Zhou land in 750, keeping the land west of Qishan.

certainty.note: No Quanrong boundary is on any page; the Qishan line is the only named limit and is soft.
